division_reconstructed.note: No source places this household anywhere — the record gives a name and no address, no street and not even a division. So BOTH halves of this band are dealt rather than read: the south division from the reconstruction order book's own household target by division, and the class from the town model's employment distribution, which puts this household under the placement policy's merchant_and_professional_dwellings clause. The better houses take the Randolph–Washington tier a block back from the trade, and the north tier under Kinzie: off the noise, on dry ground, with a garden. Inferred — the town holds one documented H roof and it is Cobweb Castle, on the north side, which is itself the clause's own outlier. The deal is seeded on this household's own id, so it is the same on every run — and it is the weakest seat this ladder makes: no lot, no roof, no coordinate and no source behind either half of it.

THE FIELD IS THE EVIDENCE UNDER THE VERDICT, not a new claim: nothing here moves the presence off `uncertain`, and T-1159 and T-1172 classify this household by this date instead of reading it out of the prose (T-1144 acceptance 9).

present_on_scene_date.note: THE CORPUS STOPS BEFORE THE SCENE DATE. Last printed 1835-06-17, at the Democrat of 17 June 1835, column 12, and nothing reached either follows this person to 1 July 1835 or says they left. A documented resident whose whereabouts on one day are unknown is `uncertain` here rather than dropped: that is the same distinction index.json draws for Jeremiah Porter, and it is a finding rather than a gap.

modelled_family.note: The kin core only. A servant, an apprentice or a journeyman this house may have held is priced by T-1183 and seated by T-1173; a boarder is seated by T-1175. The drawn size is a floor on the house.

married.what_happened: NOT DRAWN FOR THIS HOUSE: MOVED INTO IT. The household model drew this house married and the order book had no woman left in its wife's cell, so no wife was drawn. Rhoda Nichols headed a house of her own, dealt by T-1174 to fill the women and children the age pyramid lacked; she fits this house by its own rules — her division, a band never above his, no child older than his band allows — and T-2020 folds her house into his: she is his wife here and the 3 of her house come with her. Every name, age band and seed is the one T-1174 drew; the children keep the surname they were dealt with. Both people are the town's invention at the `reconstructed` tier, and the marriage is too: no source says J. W. Fell married anybody.

occupation.note: No source records an occupation for this person. This is the ABSENCE of a record rather than a claim that they did no work: the papers name them in a proceedings column, a public card or an advertisement and simply do not say what they did for a living, and `data/research/newspapers/register_1835.json` reads no trade for them. Reasoning a trade out of the company they keep would be inventing one, so the vocabulary's own word for an absent record is what stands here.

persons.note: A DOCUMENTED PERSON, AND NO TRADE IS CLAIMED BECAUSE THE PAPERS GIVE NONE. The corpus prints 'J. W. FELL' and places them at Chicago, Lake Street; it does not say what they did for a living, where this household lived, who else was in it, or when it came. The occupation therefore reads `none_recorded`, this dataset's own word for an absent record, rather than a trade reasoned from the company they keep — the absence is the finding. Cited at the Democrat of 17 June 1835, column 12. THE CORPUS GIVES AN ADDRESS IN THE TOWN — Lake Street — which is a placement no visitor passing through acquires. A place the corpus associates with a person is where the paper does business with them and not a statement about where they slept. No figure is drawn (docs/LIBERTIES.md L1). READ THROUGH A TRANSCRIPTION, not a scan: the owner's ruling of 2026-08-28 grades a transcription-mediated reading as documented, and the source record for the run states that standard and its limits. A scan read that confirms or corrects the name upgrades this entry.

age_band.note: AN AGE BAND, NEVER A YEAR. No source this project holds bears on when this person was born, so the band is drawn from the only committed sex by age distribution the project has - the 1840 Chicago schedule, five years after the scene and a town twice the size - seeded by this person's own id ('fell_j_w:age_bands_1840'). AND THE CONDITIONING IS THE MODEL'S, NOT A SOURCE'S: that a roll naming a person in their own right names somebody 15 or over. The 1840 schedule counts a child as a tally inside a household and never as a correspondent; 15 rather than 20 because an apprentice or a journeyman stands on a trade roll. No source states this rule. No exact year is written, because a year drawn from a decadal band would read as a record of a birth.

research_note: MINTED FROM THE NEWSPAPER REGISTER (T-0373) BY A RESIDENCY TEST, NOT BY A TRADE. T-0376's pass mints the register's `new_resident` people whose trade the papers print; this one takes the rest, where there is no trade to anchor anybody and a printed name on its own proves only that a Chicago paper set the type. The test asks the corpus two questions instead: does it place this person inside the town and NOWHERE outside it, and does a second independent witness corroborate a bare 'Chicago' — an address at street level, print in two or more issues, or print beside two or more people this reconstruction already holds. THE CORPUS GIVES AN ADDRESS IN THE TOWN — Lake Street — which is a placement no visitor passing through acquires. The household around them is a CONTAINER and not an argument: one member, no dwelling, no division, no family, no recorded trade, and every one of those absences written as unattested rather than filled in from the shape of the rest of the town. That the person is a HOUSEHOLD is the one invention here and it is recorded as docs/LIBERTIES.md L213. tools/mint_placed_residents.py derives the whole minted set and prints every candidate it refused, with the reason.
